title: Where Accountability Lives: Mapping Human Responsibility to Workflow Artifacts in Agentic Software Development
abstract: arXiv:2608.15678v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coding agents author commits, open pull requests, and push code in production repositories. Who is accountable is settled in two places that do not refer to each other: the platform controls that gate what an agent may do, and the provider terms that allocate responsibility for what it produces.   We read both against the workflow events that leave artifacts, across four agentic coding tools and eighteen governing policy documents from seven providers, recording at each event who holds authority, who executed and under which identity, who must verify, who bears the consequence, and which artifact survives.   The layers disagree. One provider bars the developer who assigned a task from approving the resulting pull request; another documents an agent that approves pull requests below a configured risk threshold and can dismiss reviews. translated_title: 责任何在：在代理式软件开发中将人类责任映射到工作流工件
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.15678v1 公告类型：新 摘要：编码代理在代码提交、拉取请求和生产仓库中推送代码。谁应负责这一问题在两个互不关联的地方得到解决：控制代理行为权限的平台控制机制，以及分配代理产出责任的提供商条款。我们针对这些内容与留下工件的工作流事件进行了对比分析，涉及四种代理式编码工具和七个提供商的十八份治理政策文档，记录了每个事件中谁拥有权限、谁以何种身份执行、谁必须验证、谁承担后果，以及哪个工件得以保留。各层级之间存在分歧。一个提供商禁止分配任务的开发人员批准由此产生的拉取请求；另一个提供商则记录了代理可以在配置的风险阈值以下批准拉取请求并可以驳回审查。因此，我们用强制、建议和缺失验证之间的通常三维区分替代了原有框架。
tldr: 本文通过对比四种代理编码工具和十八份政策文档，揭示了在代理式软件开发中，平台控制与提供商责任条款在关键工作流事件上存在系统性分歧，导致人类责任分配不一致。
en_tdlr: This paper compares four agentic coding tools and eighteen policy documents to reveal systematic disagreements between platform controls and provider responsibility terms at key workflow events, leading to inconsistent human accountability.
